{{nihongo|'''Miho Shrine'''|美保神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

``Miho Shrine'' is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}{{ill|Matsue|ar|ماتسوا (شيمانه)|arz|ماتسوا|az|Matsue|azb|ماتسوئه|ban|Matsué, Shimané|bar|Matsue|bg|Мацуе|ca|Matsue|ce|Мацуэ|ceb|Matsue Shi|cs|Macue|da|Matsue|de|Matsue|eo|Macuo|es|Matsue (Shimane)|et|Matsue|eu|Matsue|fa|ماتسوئه|fi|Matsue|fr|Matsue|ga|Matsue|gl|Matsue|hak|Matsue-sṳ|hu|Macue|hy|Մացուե|id|Matsue, Shimane|it|Matsue|ja|松江市|ko|마쓰에시|lt|Macujė|mg|Matsue|mzn|ماتسوئه|nl|Matsue|no|Matsue (Shimane)|pl|Matsue|pt|Matsue|ro|Matsue|ru|Мацуэ|sc|Matsue|sh|Matsue|simple|Matsue|sr|Мацуе|sv|Matsue|sw|Matsue, Shimane|tg|Матсуе|th|มัตสึเอะ|tl|Matsue|tr|Matsue|tt|Матсуе|tum|Matsue|uk|Мацуе|ur|ماتسو، شیمانے|vi|Matsue|war|Matsue, Shimane|wuu|松江市|zh|松江市|zh_classical|松江市|zh_min_nan|Matue-chhī|zh_yue|松江市|qid=Q207321}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and the former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Kokuhei Chūsha|qid=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha}}.

In addition to the divine virtue of prosperous business as Ebisu, he is also worshiped as the god of fishing and shipping, and the god of warding off insects in rice fields. Also, many {{ill|Musical instrument|Q34379|qid=Q34379}} are dedicated to the god of ``noisemono''.

=== Enshrined God ===
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami}}'s son {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi}} is enshrined in the right shrine, and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫|zh|三穗津姬|qid=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto}}, the son of Okuninushi, is enshrined in the left shrine. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of ``Omononushi-kami,'' who is the Sakimitama/Kushimitama of Okuninushi-kami. Kotoshironushi no Mikoto is the child of {{ill|Kamuyatate hime no mikoto|Q30935372|qid=Q30935372|lt=Kamuya Tatehime}} and Okuninushi, so she is her stepmother.

In ``{{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}},'' there is a description that ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mihosusumi no Mikoto}},'' born between Ōanamochi no Mikoto (Okuninushi deity) and Nunasenamihime no Mikoto ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawahime no Mikoto}}), sits in Mihosato. Originally, the only deity enshrined at our company was Mihosumi-no-Mikoto, but it seems that due to the influence of {{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|Q842308|qid=Q842308}}{{ill|Japanese mythology|Q814158|qid=Q814158|lt=Mythology}}, Kotoshiro-nushi-kami and Mihotsu-hime-no-Mikoto were enshrined.

=== History ===
The origin of its founding is unknown, but it is an old shrine listed in the shrine register of ``{{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}'' compiled in {{ill|8th century|Q8086|qid=Q8086}}. In {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, you line up at a small shrine.

From {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, {{ill|Yokoyama clan|Q119822420|qid=Q119822420}} became {{ill|Kannushi|Q60523|qid=Q60523}} {{ill|Line of hereditary succession|Q756689|qid=Q756689}}. From around {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, it was said that ``Taisha ({{ill|Izumo-taisha|Q696362|qid=Q696362}}) alone is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=one visit}},'' and the number of worshipers started to increase along with Izumo Taisha. Together with Izumo Taisha Shrine, it is collectively known as ``Izumo's Ebisu Daikoku''.

In {{ill|1885|Q7821|qid=Q7821}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}18), it was listed as Kokupei Chusha, and after {{ill|World War II|Q362|qid=Q362}} it became {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

</gallery>{{ill|2023|Q49622|qid=Q49622}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}}5) The current main shrine was built after a fire in {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}}12 ({{ill|1800|Q6875|qid=Q6875}}). (era name)|Q1373146|Bunka 10th year}} ({{ill|1813|Q6937|qid=Q6937}}) <ref name="Nonomura 2002p68">{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nonomura 2002}}, p. 68</ref>. It is a special form of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|qid=Q387874}} with two consecutive buildings on the left and right sides, and is called ``Miho-zukuri'' or ``Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'' and is designated as an important cultural property of the country. It is not clear when this style was established<ref name="Nonomura 2002p68"/>. {{ill|Hōreki|Q1194397|qid=Q1194397}} In a document called "Haku-sama Goyo no Kaku" written in 1763, {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} The company name is written as ``Miho''' Shrine'''' in the 3rd year (1534) article, and ``Miho'''Ryosha'''' in the 11th year (1583) article. Also, according to the "Kokuhei Chusha Miho Shrine Detailed Book" written in {{ill|1886|Q7822|qid=Q7822}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}19), for {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}} years ({{ill|1570|Q6659|qid=Q6659}} - There was only one main shrine until it was lost in the war in {{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}), but after that, for {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}} ({{ill|1593|Q6772|qid=Q6772}} - Until {{ill|1596|Q6785|qid=Q6785}}), it was rebuilt as it is today, with two main halls built on one foundation.<ref name="Nonomura 2002p68"/> From these two documents, it is estimated that as of the 3rd year of Tenbun ({{ill|1534|Q6447|qid=Q6447}}), it was a single-building shrine, and by the 11th year of Tensho ({{ill|1583|Q6726|qid=Q6726}}), it had become a two-building shrine called ``Ryosha.''<ref name="Nonomura 2002p68"/> In addition, {{ill|Kikkawa Hiroie|Q1049766|qid=Q1049766|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa}}, which was recorded as an auspicious day in May in {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}} 5th year ({{ill|1596|Q6785|qid=Q6785}}), is {{ja link|Bunroku-Keicho War|Q576338|When the building was built for the dispatch of troops to Korea}}, the ridge plate also read ``Hokenri Mihonoseki'''Ryo'' Shrine Palace, which proves that two shrine buildings were already standing side by side at that time<ref name="Nonomura2002p68"/>. However, it is unknown whether the two shrine buildings at that time were connected as they are now<ref name="Nonomura 2002p68"/>. Due to repairs in {{ill|1928|Q19715|qid=Q19715}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}3), the main shrine was moved about 100 meters from its original location to its current location, and the sacred area was expanded to complete its current form. 2002}}, p. 70</ref>. The roofs of the main shrine, worship hall, shrine gate, corridors, and entrance walls are currently {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477|lt=cypress bark}}, but before the repair, they were shingle roofs<ref name="Nonomura 2002p70"/>. There is a subsidiary shrine and Daigosha between the two main shrines, and three shrines and five shrines (Daigosha {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiya Tatehime no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Nunakawahime|Q11142832|qid=Q11142832|lt=Numakawa Hime no Mikoto}}, Himeko Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himekeka Isuzuhime no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Isuzuyori-hime|Q10881557|qid=Q10881557}}, Jinshisha Inasehime no Mikoto) is enshrined here.

=== Festival ===
The Aofushigaki ritual and the {{ill|Morotebune|Q11632096|qid=Q11632096}} (Morotabune) ritual originate from the {{ill|Kuni-yuzuri|Q11621119|qid=Q11621119|lt=Kokuyoshi myth}}. The Morotefune ritual in December reenacts the story of {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Okuninushi-no-Mikoto|UNKNOWN|qid=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami}} sending a messenger to his son {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotodai-nushi-kami}} to consult with him about the pros and cons of ceding the country, and the Aoshibagaki-gaki ritual in April, where Kotodai-nushi-kami, who had decided to cede the country, changed his ship into an Ao-shibagaki fence and carried it inside. He hides himself, but recreates the scene of being resurrected as a god again. {{ja icon}} - Suntory Channel, 2014</ref>. Our two members, who have avoided eating chicken, chicken, and eggs for a year and purified themselves at sea every day, fasted the day before, boarded two boats decorated with blue shibagaki, and after circling the port, visited Miho Shrine and offered offerings. Mihonoseki Regional Tourism Promotion Council official website</ref>.

* {{ill|January 1|Q2150|qid=Q2150}} -- Saitan Festival
* {{ill|January 7|Q2228|qid=Q2228}} -- First Ebisu Festival
* Mid-January--Firecracker Ceremony (Tondo-san) [[File:Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony.jpg|Thumbnail|Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony]]
* February Setsubun -- Setsubun Festival* {{ill|April 7|Q2505|qid=Q2505}} -- Reitaisai (Aoshibagaki Shinto Ritual): The Reitaisai is held in the morning, and the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual is held in the afternoon.
* {{ill|April 13|Q2498|qid=Q2498}} -- Fishing Festival
* {{ill|May 5|Q2550|qid=Q2550}} -- Shinto ritual

* {{ill|December 3|Q2298|qid=Q2298}} -- Niiname-sai/Morotebune ritual

=== Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei ===
; Namisaki Gohei
: Dedicated at the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual.
; Monthly gohei
: It is offered during the monthly festival on the 7th of every month.

=== Transportation ===
{{ill|Matsue Station|Q1058652|qid=Q1058652}} From platform 2, take the {{ill|Ichibata Bus|Q11352955|qid=Q11352955}} bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (about 40 minutes). From the Mihonoseki terminal end, transfer to the {{ill|Mihonoseki community bus|Q11531653|qid=Q11531653|lt=Mihonoseki community bus}} bound for {{ill|Mihonoseki, Shimane|Q6845336|qid=Q6845336|lt=Mihonoseki}} and get off at the Mihonoseki terminal (about 30 minutes). About 1 minute walk from Miho Shrine Iriguchi bus stop.

{{ill|Hatsumōde|Q1032381|qid=Q1032381}} season, {{ill|Golden Week (Japan)|Q1137351|qid=Q1137351}}, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays from summer to early winter, and {{ill|December 3|Q2298|qid=Q2298}}, {{ill|Q115 04700|qid=Q115 04700|lt=Hinomaru Bus}} operates the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" between {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yonago Airport}} and {{ill|Sakaiminato Station|Q7402786|qid=Q7402786}}<ref>[http://mihojinja.or.jp/kotsu/#anchor0 [Limited Time] Ebisu Liner] - Miho Shrine (viewed March 8, 2019). </ref>.

There is a parking lot next to the community center (free of charge, with space for more than a dozen cars) and a public toilet, and it is a 1-minute walk from the shrine.
